note: Rows Spotrac published wrong, keyed by date|player|type. Applied by scrape-transactions.mjs after every merge, so the feed on disk is right no matter how many times it is re-pulled, and the wrong row never has to be hand-edited twice. Each entry says what Spotrac printed, what the corrected text is, and where the correction comes from. Remove an entry once Spotrac fixes the row. An entry may also carry `newDate`, which re-dates the row: the feed keeps a trade on the day it was agreed even when the league approved it months later.

corrections.detail: Traded to Minnesota (MIN) from Utah (UTA) as part of a 2-team trade: Minnesota (MIN) traded Josh Green and cash to Utah (UTA); Utah (UTA) traded Cody Williams and John Konchar to Minnesota (MIN)
corrections.why: Spotrac's row reads 'Traded to Utah (UTA) from Minnesota (MIN) as part of a 1-team trade:' for all three players and lists no legs. Green went to Utah; Williams and Konchar came to Minnesota (ESPN, RealGM, NBA.com, Aug 29). Spotrac's own Jazz apron figure confirms the direction to the dollar: $178,017,268 + Green $14,679,012 − Konchar $6,165,000 − Williams $6,015,600 = $180,515,680, the number their tracker prints.

corrections.detail: LA (LAC) withdrew Qualifying Offer with his consent; becomes an Unrestricted Free Agent
corrections.why: Spotrac attributes the withdrawal to New Orleans, the team he signed with. The Clippers held the qualifying offer and withdrew it with his consent so he could sign in New Orleans (Aug 26).

corrections.detail: Agreed to a 1 year $3.52 million contract with Sacramento Kings (SAC)
corrections.why: Spotrac's row reads 'with LA Clippers (LAC)', which is the team he last played for (18 games in 2024-25), not the team he signed with. NBA.com ('Reports: Ben Simmons agrees to one-year deal with Kings'), NBC Sports (Spears) and Yahoo all have Sacramento on Sep 4 2026, one year at the veteran minimum — $3.52M is the 9-YOS figure ($3,524,115) to the dollar. Entry comes out when Spotrac fixes theirs.

corrections.detail: Signed a 1 year $3.52 million contract with Sacramento Kings (SAC)
corrections.why: Spotrac's 'Signed' row repeats the Sep 4 mistake: 'with LA Clippers (LAC)'. The Kings announced the signing themselves on Sep 8 (NBA.com: 'Kings officially sign Ben Simmons to one-year deal'; Yahoo, CBS), and Spotrac's own Sacramento apron figure rose by exactly $2,449,421 on the same pull — the Art. VII §3(f) charge for a one-year veteran minimum. Entry comes out when Spotrac fixes theirs.

corrections.detail: Traded to Toronto (TOR) from LA (LAC) for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, a 2027 1st round pick [TOR right to swap] , a 2031 1st round pick [unprotected] , a 2033 1st round pick [unprotected] , a 2030 2nd round pick and a 2033 2nd round pick
corrections.why: Completed Sep 14, 2026. The trade was agreed on Jun 30, paused by Toronto on Jul 9 while the league investigated Leonard's off-court money, and completed on Sep 14 once the Sep 2 ruling left his contract intact — 76 days after the agreement (Hoops Rumors, Sep 14; Shams Charania; Law Murray of The Athletic: terms unchanged, Leonard waived his 15% trade kicker). Spotrac keeps the row on the agreement date; RealGM's pick ledger dates every pick in the deal 9/14/2026. The sheet dates the trade the day it was executed, so the Sep 14 news day carries it and a rewind to any day before shows the rosters the league recognized.

corrections.detail: Signed a 1 year $2.63 million contract with Portland (POR) via Exhibit 9
corrections.why: Spotrac's row reads 'Signed a 1 year $2.63 million a contract with Portland (POR)' with no camp label, but Hoops Rumors (Aug 2, 'Trail Blazers, Jeremy Sochan Complete One-Year Deal') has the deal non-guaranteed at the veteran minimum, a training-camp spot to compete for alongside Micah Potter and Vit Krejci; Spotrac's own Portland cap page and apron figure leave him off.
